newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower after drifting in range.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower after drifting in range.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed lower on Friday having traded in a fairly narrow range with the market still hesitant after Thursday's 90 cent slump, dealers said.
Dec Brent closed five cents off an intra-day low at $22.50 a barrel, 17 cents down on the day. The contract briefly brushed a session high of $22.84 shortly after trade on NYMEX began.
"The market was really a bit shell-shocked after yesterday," said one broker.
"There wasn't much impetus in either direction, we just took our cues from NYMEX."
NYMEX crude tested, but left unbreached, key support at $23.

Friday's statement from the United States Ambassador to the United Nations, Madeleine Albright, saying that Iraq was making "outrageous demands" over the implementation of the U.N./Iraq oil-for-food agreement, failed to jolt the market higher.
"(Iraq) wasn't the reason the market came off yesterday, so it didn't push it up again today," said an IPE floor broker.
On Thursday, two rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq, where recent clashes have made it unsafe for U.N. monitors, agreed to extend a U.S.-brokered cease-fire.
"The funds moved out because prices were high and they lost their bottle, not on these bits of (Iraqi) news," said a dealer.
